original_question: Given a non-trivial virtual knot K, can one prove that there exists a minimal realization of K in a thickened surface N = S_g x I together with an unknotted embedding of N into R^3 such that the resulting classical knot in R^3 is non-trivial?
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation: it has the correct hypothesis (a non-trivial virtual knot K), the correct ambient 3-manifold N = S_g × I, the correct requirement of an unknotted embedding N ⊂ R^3, and the correct conclusion that the induced classical knot in R^3 should be non-trivial. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should say that "non-trivial" means non-trivial as a virtual knot, i.e. not equivalent to the virtual unknot in the virtual/stable-equivalence sense used in the paper. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

It should define "minimal realization" as a realization of K in S_g × I where the genus g is minimal among all thickened-surface realizations representing K; the paper’s nearby discussion ties this to Kuperberg’s minimal-genus representative in a stable class. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

It should specify that S_g is a compact oriented surface of genus g and that I is an interval (typically taken to be a closed interval). The paper introduces virtual knots through embeddings in thickened surfaces S_g × R, and Problem 19 specializes to N = S_g × I. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

It should make explicit that the realization is understood in the thickened-surface model of virtual knot theory, where two such realizations represent the same virtual knot up to isotopy in thickened surfaces, surface homeomorphisms, and addition/removal of empty handles. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

It should clarify that the "obtained classical knot in R^3" is the image of the chosen minimal surface realization of K under the specified embedding e: N ↪ R^3. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

There are no ambient ring/field choices, degree restrictions, homogeneity assumptions, nilpotency conditions, or asymptotic quantifiers in this problem; it is a purely topological existence question. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
refined_question: Let K be a non-trivial virtual knot, interpreted via the thickened-surface model as a stable equivalence class of knot embeddings in surfaces times an interval. Does there exist a realization of K as a knot in N = S_g × I, where S_g is a compact oriented surface of minimal possible genus among all such realizations of K, together with an unknotted embedding e: N ↪ R^3, such that the image e(K) is a non-trivial classical knot in R^3? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 19 essentially verbatim, not a broader neighboring problem. The precise problem statement appears in Section 7 under "Embeddings of Surfaces." The needed hidden context comes from Section 2.2, where the paper interprets virtual knots as stable equivalence classes of links in thickened surfaces, and from the later discussion that cites Kuperberg’s uniqueness of the minimal-genus embedding in a stable class. The paper also records, in the statement of Problem 19 itself and the references, that the problem was partially solved by Heather Dye. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
